motivation: In 2008 Hosono's group reported superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO. This was a family nobody expected, since iron magnetism was thought to destroy superconductivity. Within weeks, Chen at USTC and Zhao at IOP-CAS replaced lanthanum with rare earths and raised Tc above 40 K and then to 55 K. That was the first non-cuprate family to clearly exceed the conventional 'McMillan limit' at ambient pressure. The discovery opened a second class of high-temperature superconductors, now numbering hundreds of compounds. It showed that unconventional pairing arising from magnetism is a general organising principle and not something peculiar to cuprates. It revealed electronic nematicity, sign-changing multiband pairing and quantum criticality in materials clean enough for decisive experiments. It also produced FeSe monolayers and practical high-field wires. Like the cuprates, it is a defining case of new materials transforming what physicists believe is possible.
